newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BLEARY-EYED DORTMUNDERS READY FOR FRESH PARTY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BLEARY-EYED DORTMUNDERS READY FOR FRESH PARTY.

text.p: The citizens of Dortmund woke up bleary eyed on Thursday after a giant all-night party and promptly prepared to celebrate all over again -- to welcome home their European Cup-winning heroes.

Police said tens of thousands of Dortmund's 600,000 residents had taken part in late-night festivities in and around the Friedensplatz central square, where Wednesday's final was relayed live from Munich on a giant video screen.
Some fans had not even gone to bed and intended to keep on partying through the day.
"I drank, drank and drank and I waved my flag," declared Marco Neumann, a welder from the nearby city of Essen as he lounged over a fairground carousel in the centre of Dortmund.
"You only experience this sort of thing once," said Neumann, waving a huge flag in the Dortmund colours of bright yellow and black at passers-by.
A police spokesman praised the Dortmund fans for their discipline, reporting just 10 detentions for drunkenness and only one arrest -- for stealing a Dortmund scarf.

Borussia's 3-1 win over Juventus completed a remarkable double for Germany's depressed Ruhe Valley industrial heartland after neigbours Schalke won the UEFA Cup last week by beating another top-class Italian side -- Internazionale of Milan.
"For many people, Borussia isn't a football club, it's a way of looking at the world," said Mirvais Karzai, a local hotel manager. "They identify with Borussia to the absolute limit."
The triumph could not have come at a better time for those intent on celebrating in style. Most Dortmunders had Thursday off work anyway because of the Corpus Christi public holiday.
"The mood was superb. It beats anything else," said Mike Brueckner, an unemployed construction worker who had travelled from eastern Germany to watch the game in Dortmund.
The city was due to greet the players with a motorcade followed by a reception for the team at the Friedensplatz.
Local and national newspapers splashed black and yellow headlines across their front pages to proclaim Germany's first European Cup triumph since 1983.
"Borussissima!" declared Bild, Germany's best-selling newspaper, with some creative use of the Italian language to describe its feelings. "We're the kings of Europe."
"The dream has come true!" commented Dortmund's main local newspaper, the Westdeutsche Allgemeine Zeitung.
"Borussia, this is madness!" the Ruhr Nachrichten daily yelled.
